survey: Image 4 is a water slide on a tiled pool deck. A yellow square platform with a post railing sits on one yellow pole. The pole stands on a round, flat base disc on the deck, and a diagonal brace runs from the pole up to the platform's underside. A blue ladder leans from the platform's front-right edge down to the deck, with both feet on the tiles. A green slide leaves the platform at its left side, turns left and down, and passes in front of the pole. It then swings out to the right and comes back across the front of the pole. It ends at the pool's edge, where its water pours into the pool. The whole scene is seen from one raised three-quarter view from the front: you can see the platform's top, the inside of the slide channel at every turn, and the tiles. The base disc, the post tops and the pool edge are ellipses of about the same flatness, which fits a ground seen at that angle. The deck tile rows follow the ground plane and bend with the pool's edge. The pole stays vertical. The ladder's two side rails stay parallel, and its rungs keep a steady size and tilt along the rails. Where the slide crosses the pole, it overlaps it in a way that fits a spiral wrapping around it. The pole base and ladder feet sit flat on the deck, and the slide's exit lines up with the pool's edge.
